correctness.rationale: The determinant factorization is an exact algebraic identity. At \(a=1/4\), zero-delay Hurwitz stability is certified by exact rational determinants; the quartic root geometry reduces to a strictly monotone cubic in \(x^2\); all four positive imaginary crossing frequencies and their first phase-compatible delays are enumerated. The first is \(\omega_*=0.705570557982711\ldots\), \(\theta_*=0.876243533775502\ldots\), with positive crossing speed \(0.147965713761474\ldots\). The source value \(2.0083\) is excluded from the exhaustive frequency set. The bundled verifier reconstructs the critical computation. The proved limit is linear stability only.

value.rationale: The finding exposes a reusable scalar factorization of a four-dimensional delay characteristic determinant, gives the complete positive crossing-frequency set, and corrects a published numerical benchmark. This changes the precise delay margin and shows that the reported frequency is impossible for the printed model, while retaining the source simulations as a valid coarse bracket. That is a substantive structural and diagnostic result rather than a routine decimal refinement.
